b: This weekend the American Heart Association posted a compelling story of Alex L who, at age 53, underwent a screening coronary artery scan. I will screenshot the now deleted post below.
It’s a compelling story, one repeated on social media often. It’s led many the influencer to recommend getting a CAC scan because it could save your life.
But that is not what the evidence shows. A swift and robust response from many practicing cardiologists led the AHA to delete the post.

For today’s post, I thought I would give a gift to subscribers and lay out the evidence why such a compelling story is not backed by the evidence.

I will first show you the screening trials. then the PCI or stent trials, and then the surgery trials. The intervention trials were comparison to medical therapy initially with allowance for crossover to intervention when symptoms developed. Note that Alex had no symptoms.

Before I get into the evidence, I should say what the CAC proponents recommend in guidelines for CAC use. Simply stated, the scan is supposed to help people in intermediate risk categories decide on statin therapy. An intermediate risk person (say around 7% at 10 years who has a high CAC might be motivated to take a statin whereas that same person with a CAC 0 might feel ok in not taking statins. That is it. No expert recommends cascade testing as depicted in Alex L’s story.
